sentences.text:
. 
Learned counsel for the petitioner/convict/A-2 would submit that the petitioner/appellant was found guilty for the offence under Sections 342, 376-D, 394, 506 and 323 IPC and convicted U/s.235(2) Cr.P.C. and he was sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of one (01) year and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- (Rupees One Thousand only), in default of payment of fine, A-2 has to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 15 days for the offence U/s.342 IPC.

The petitioner/convict/A-2 is sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of twenty (20) years and to pay a fine of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only), in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of three (03) months for the offence Contd.,2 under Section 376-D IPC.

The petitioner/convict/A-2 is sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten (10) years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only),
in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of one (01) month for the offence under Section 394 IPC.

The petitioner/convict/A-2 is sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of two (02) years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/-
(Rupees Five Thousand only), in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of one (01)
month for the offence under Section 506 IPC.

The petitioner/convict/A-2 is sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of one (01) year and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- (Rupees One Thousand only), in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of 15 days for the offence under Section 323 IPC.
All the sentences shall run concurrently.
The petitioner/appellant filed application to suspend the sentence, pending disposal of the appeal.

Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed the application contending that during the trial, bail of the appellant was cancelled, as he was violated the conditions and the alleged offence is a grave offence, Contd.,3 :: 3 ::

sentences.text: He would further submit that the petitioner involved in 12 more criminal cases, and opposed the application.
Undisputedly, the appellant/convict/A-2 was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for a period of twenty (20) years for the offence under Section 376-D of Indian Penal Code, 1860.

Before parting with the matter, this Court would like to note that the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Lilaben Vs. State of Gujarat and Others1, which is a case under POCSO Act 2012, observed that "sentence imposed for 20 years is greater than life imprisonment".

Accordingly, the application is dismissed.
